text:
amira: Customer SQ asks: "Do you ever log customer prompts/PII in system logs? Which subprocessors can access logs and how are access approvals handled?" Need a short, clear answer to paste into the form. cc @tim @jordan

tim: Short answer: default telemetry does NOT include full prompt text or customer PII. We capture request_id, model, token counts, status, latency, and error codes. Prompt contents are not sent to the aggregated telemetry pipeline by default.

sec-bot: FYI internal KB: https://redwood.internal/security/logs-pii (links only accessible internally)

jordan: To expand slightly for the CSQ: we only persist full request bodies in two cases — 1) customer-enabled debug/replay mode, or 2) when a debug capture is manually triggered for an incident. Those captures are stored in an encrypted log-archive with restricted access.

rebecca: For subprocessors: the types of vendors that may touch logs are cloud storage (e.g., our S3 buckets), our ingestion/archival pipeline (log-archive service), and our monitoring/alerting partner used for production metrics. The canonical list is in the subprocessors appendix we share with customers.

tim: Example of access control/process: full-log access requires a triage ticket, an engineering owner approval, AND a security approval. All accesses are audited and logged. Encryption: logs are encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest using KMS; for Private deployments we can use customer-managed KMS.

jordan: Also include retention numbers in the answer: default telemetry retention is 30 days; debug captures default to 90 days and are configurable per-customer.

rebecca: Draft wording for CSQ (one paragraph): "By default, Redwood does not include customer prompt contents or identifiable PII in its aggregated telemetry. Full request bodies are only retained when a customer enables debug/replay or when a capture is explicitly triggered for troubleshooting; these captures are encrypted at rest (KMS), access-controlled, and audited. Subprocessors that may handle logs are limited to our cloud storage providers, our log ingestion/archival service, and our monitoring partner; we provide a current subprocessors list and SOC2 evidence upon request."

amira: This is great — I will paste that into the questionnaire. @sec-bot can you attach the current subprocessors list and the SOC2 report?

sec-bot: Attached: /security/subprocessors-current-2025.pdf, /security/soc2-report-2024.pdf :paperclip:

tim: Optional small config snippet they sometimes ask for (how we redact by default):

```
redact:
  - path: request.prompt
    mode: hash
  - path: user.email
    mode: remove
```

jordan: :thumbsup: Looks good. amira — if they ask about encryption algorithms we generally state AES-256-GCM for at-rest KMS wrapping.

amira: Thanks everyone — sending back to the customer now.
